https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/nato-figh.text: Charlie Bradley Updated Sun, September 13, 2026 at 12:47 PM UTC 0 NATO fighter jets (Image: Getty) NATO fighter jets have been scrambled amid reports that a Russian drone was headed for Lithuania, but this was later confirmed to be a flock of birds. Flights were suspended at Vilnius Airport in the country's capital, and the Lithuanian National Crisis Management Centre issued a yellow alert for possible drone hazard in Vilnius, Trakai, and Elektrenai districts. The air alert has since been lifted by authorities. Vilmantas Vitkauskas, head of the National Crisis Management Center, said after the alert: "There is no threat, people can calm down. (...) In principle, the threat level has been eliminated." According to the Lithuanian Armed Forces, radars near Varna detected an object moving towards the Kaliningrad region. Authorities later confirmed: "Fighter jets carrying out a NATO air policing mission were deployed to inspect the object. They determined that the radar signals were a flock of birds." The Lithuanian military said earlier this week that drones aimed at Ukraine have landed in Lithuanian territory. Commander of the Armed Forces of Lithuania General Raimundas Vaikšnoras confirmed that Russian "Gerbera" drones were originally fired at Ukrainian cities before landing in Lithuania. Vilnius Airport (Image: Getty) Russia has issued numerous threats to Lithuania as the country continues to boost its defences amid fears it could be attacked by Moscow's forces. Just this week, former Russian President Dmitry Medvedev suggested wiping Lithuania "off the map." He said: "No one will come to their defence. Even if the place is reduced to scorched earth, no other country will go to war for them. And the well-known Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty - it will not be invoked, everyone recognises that. Because if it is invoked, it will be a global catastrophe, a planetary one. They are not fools.
